div.head: Rect 2
div.ab: [2] Geneates riht. Geneatriht is mistlic be ðam ðe on lande stænt: on sumon he sceal landgafol syllan ⁊ gærsswyn on geare ⁊ ridan ⁊ auerian ⁊ lade lædan, wyrcan ⁊ hlaford feormian, ripan ⁊ mawan, deorhege heawan ⁊ sæte haldan, bytlian ⁊ burh hegegian, nigefaran to tune feccan, cyricsceat syllan ⁊ ælmesfeoh, heafodwearde healdan ⁊ horswearde, ærendian fyr swa nyr, swa hwyder swa him mon to tæcð.

(Uillani.) Uillani rectum est uarium et multiplex, secundum quod in terra statutum est: in quibusdam terris debet dare landgablum et gærssþin (id est porcum herbagii) et equitare et aueriare et summagium ducere, operari et dominum suum firmare, metere et falcare, deorhege cedere et stabilitatem obseruare, edificare et circumsepire, nouam faram adducere, ciricsceattum dare et ælmesfeoh (id est pecuniam elemosine), heafodwardam custodire et horswardam, in nuntium ire longe uel prope, quocumque dicetur ei.

GE NEATES RIHT . Geneat riht is mistlic be ðam ðe onlan|de stænt . on sumon he sceal land gafol syllan 7 gærsswyn . on geare . 7 ridan 7 auerian 7 lade lædan. wyrcan . 7 hlaford feormian. ripan 7 mawan . deorhege heawan. 7 sæte haldan .bytlian . 7 burh hegegian nigefaran to tune feccan . cyricsceat syllan . 7 ælmes feoh . heafod|wearde healdan .7 horswearde . ærendi|an . fyr . swa nyr . swa hwyder swa him mon to tæcð.

Geneates riht Geneatriht is mistlic be ðam ðe on lande stænt. On summon, he sceal landgafol syllan and gærsswyn on geare and ridan and averian and lade lædan, wyrcan and hlaford feormian, ripan and mawan, deorhege heawan and sæte haldan, bytlian and burh hegegian, nigefaran to tune feccan, cyricsceat syllan and ælmesfeoh, heafodwearde healdan and horswearde, ærendian fyr swa nyr, swa hwyder swa him mon to tæcð.

Rechtspflicht des Geneat. Geneatpflicht ist verschieden, je nachdem es auf dem Landgute [hofrechtlich] gilt: auf einigen [Gütern] muss er Grundzins zahlen und jährlich ein Schwein als Gras[rechtsentgelt], und reiten und Pferde-Spanndienst leisten, Transportladung führen, [in Frohn] arbeiten und dem [Guts]herrn Gastung leisten, Ernte schneiden und [Heu] mähen, Wildgehege zuhauen und Fangvorrichtung halten, Baudienst leisten und das Herrenhaus [Domänengehöft] umfestigen, fremde Ankömmlinge zum Gutsdorfe holen, Kirchensteuer zahlen und Almosengeld, Leibwache [beim Herrn] halten und Pferdebewachung, Botschaft tragen fern wie nah, wohin immer ihm zugewiesen wird.

The duty of the geneat [the personally free peasant under a lord's estate]. The geneat's duty varies according to what holds on the estate [by custom]: on some [estates] he must pay [the lord] land-rent and yearly a pig as grass-[rent], and ride and do carrying service with horses, carry loads, work [in labour-service] and provide the [estate-]lord with hospitality, reap and mow, cut the deer-fence [for the lord's hunting] and maintain the hunting-stand, do building work and fence the manor-house, fetch strangers to the village, pay church-scot and alms-money, keep guard [at the lord's side] and guard horses, carry messages far or near, wherever he is directed.

The duty of the tenant The duty of the tenant is diverse, according to [the customs] that stand on the estate. In some he must pay land tax and a pasturage pig each year, and ride and provide horses for team work and carry loads, labour, provide food for the lord, reap and mow, cut the animal-hedge, and maintain snares, build and fence the dwellings within an enclosure, and lead newcomers to the enclosure, pay church tribute and alms money, hold head-guard (duties) and guard horses, go on errands, either further or nearer or to wherever he is sent.

The Duty of the Tenant The tenant’s duty varies according to what is practiced on the estate. On some, he must pay rent on the land, and give a pig for the use of the pasture each year, and ride and act as his lord’s messenger, and carry loads, work, and supply food for his lord, reap and mow, trim the animal hedge, assist in ensnaring game, build and erect a fence around the homestead, guide newcomers to the community, pay Church dues and alms, serve as a guard to the lord and to the horses, carry out errands both far and near or to wherever he is instructed to go.
div.note: Liebermann compares the customs of Tidenham, Gloucestershire (Bath cartulary, c. 1050), and Rect 4.1c and 4a.; AU: corrected against Rabin p. 316 / 317, October 2026 (was “andorswearde,; h”, now “and horswearde,; ∅”)

ride and act as his lord’s messenger: Literally, “provide carrying service.” There is disagreement over the meaning of this term, with some scholars arguing that it refers to the tenant’s duty to provide horses for plowing. However, the likelihood that Old English averian is to be derived from Latin averagium (service by horse to one’s lord) as well as its possible relationship to Old English aferian (to move or take), makes the translation used here more plausible.

Vgl. Gl Bauer 5; Abgabe 7. 9—15. Nur der Viertelhufner zahlt landgafol auf Gütern Londons; Hale Domesday of S. Paul's p. lxix. Dieser Zins ist zu scheiden von Fronablösung, Kopfsteuer, Hilfsgeld zu besonderer Gelegenheit und von staatlicher Steuer; vgl. d. Gl 4; Vinogradoff Villain. 292f.

Cf. Gl Bauer 5; Abgabe 7. 9—15. On the London estates only the holder of a quarter-hide pays landgafol; Hale Domesday of S. Paul's p. lxix. This rent is to be distinguished from the commutation of labour services, poll tax, aid on special occasions, and state taxation; cf. that word in Gl 4; Vinogradoff Villain. 292f.

Nicht ‘pastured pig’ (Sweet), oder ‘Weideschwein’ (Leo, Schmid); auch in gærsyrð heisst gærs ‘Grasentgelt, Leistung für Heu’; s. d. Gl 5. In Londoner Gutsrecht kommt garsavese (s. Wb: æfesn) vor; Hale (o. ³) lxviij. Vgl. Neilson Customary rents 68. Herbagium sagt Q dafür auch 4, 1b

Not ‘pastured pig’ (Sweet), or ‘pasture pig’ (Leo, Schmid); in gærsyrð too gærs means ‘payment for grass, render for hay’; see that word in Gl 5. In London estate custom garsavese (see Wb: æfesn) occurs; Hale (above ³) lxviij. Cf. Neilson Customary rents 68. Q also renders it Herbagium at 4, 1b

Das Wort trennt Toller Suppl. jetzt von áferian und verbindet es richtig mit eafor. Vgl. Gl Pferd 1a. 2; mein Abfass. der Rect. und ags. ‘eafor’ in Archiv Stud. neu. Spra. 109, 75. [Nachtrag zu S. 81⁶ average: Skeat Etymol. dict. s. v.]

Toller Suppl. now separates the word from áferian and rightly connects it with eafor. Cf. Gl Pferd 1a. 2; my Abfass. der Rect. und ags. ‘eafor’ in Archiv Stud. neu. Spra. 109, 75. [Addendum to p. 81⁶ average: Skeat Etymol. dict. s. v.]
‘Saumrosse’ zu eng Leo; leading ‘Ernte einfahren’ Larking Domesday of Kent 165; Boden, der hierzu pflichtig ist, heisst lodland; Vinogradoff Villainage 257
‘pack-horses’ is too narrow, Leo; leading ‘carting in the harvest’ Larking Domesday of Kent 165; land liable to this is called lodland; Vinogradoff Villainage 257
Nicht ‘zu religiösen Festschmäusen beitragen’ (Leo); vgl. Gl Gastung Z. 10 und n. 5a
Not ‘contribute to religious feasts’ (Leo); cf. Gl Gastung l. 10 and n. 5a
Vgl. Gl Heu; Fron 2. 4. Ceorlas sculan don to Hysseburnan . . healfne æcer gauolmæde; Birch 594. Ausser zur Schnittzeit hat der Geneat die ganze Woche frei. Vgl. Andrews Manor 154
Cf. Gl Heu; Fron 2. 4. Ceorlas sculan don to Hysseburnan . . healfne æcer gauolmæde; Birch 594. Except at reaping time the geneat has the whole week free. Cf. Andrews Manor 154
‘Staken zum Wildzaune’ Leo. Im Ger 12 fürs Frühjahr angesetzt. Vgl. o. 1, 1³. Die Jagd des Thegn scheint gemeint (nicht die des Königs, so dass der Geneat die Gutslast des Thegn verträte)

‘stakes for the game fence’ Leo. In Ger 12 it is assigned to the spring. Cf. above 1, 1³. The thegn's hunting seems to be meant (not the king's, in which case the geneat would be discharging the thegn's estate obligation on his behalf)
für des Herrn Jagd
for the lord's hunting

Vgl. Gl Jagd 6e. Toller 812 versteht ungenau ‘places from which the deer might be shot’, ähnlich Stubbs Select char., Gloss.: stabilitio. Nicht ‘Zäune, Weidegehege’ (Leo) oder ‘in Ordnung halten’ (Schmid). Sæt heisst ‘Hinterhalt’, sætian ‘auflauern’, sætere ‘Nachsteller’, sætung : aucupatio ‘Schlinge’. Im Königsforst mussten unter Heinrich I. Einwohner ad stabilitam venire; Hn 17. Stabulata quibus in casses cervi urgentur erwähnt Will. Malmesbur. Reg. II 191, ed. Stubbs p. 236

Cf. Gl Jagd 6e. Toller 812 inaccurately understands ‘places from which the deer might be shot’, and similarly Stubbs Select char., Gloss.: stabilitio. Not ‘fences, pasture enclosures’ (Leo) or ‘keep in order’ (Schmid). Sæt means ‘ambush’, sætian ‘to lie in wait’, sætere ‘pursuer’, sætung : aucupatio ‘snare’. Under Henry I inhabitants of the royal forest were obliged ad stabilitam venire; Hn 17. Stabulata quibus in casses cervi urgentur are mentioned by Will. Malmesbur. Reg. II 191, ed. Stubbs p. 236

cf. Gerefa 9: bytlian

Nicht ‘neue Fähre herbeischaffen’ (Leo) oder ‘neue Wege machen’ (Kemble, Schmid, Andrews). Auch faru heisst nicht ‘Fähre’ oder ‘Strasse’. Q versteht das Wort nicht.—Vielmehr vgl. gefara ‘(Reise)gefährte’, merefara ‘Seefahrer’, nydfara ‘Zwangsgänger’, tidfara ‘Zeitwanderer’, nifara ‘Ankömmling, Fremder’, nige-cerred, -cumen, -hwirfed, -hworfen, niwan come (Beda II 1), -cumen. Der adventicius, forinsecus, extraneus darf ins Manor 13. Jhs. nicht ohne Erlaubnis des Gutsherrn einwandern, sondern wird erst zum Domänenhof geleitet; Vinogradoff Villainage 159. 142f. Vgl. Gl Dorf 5b

Not ‘procure a new ferry’ (Leo) or ‘make new roads’ (Kemble, Schmid, Andrews). Nor does faru mean ‘ferry’ or ‘road’. Q does not understand the word.—Rather, cf. gefara ‘(travelling) companion’, merefara ‘seafarer’, nydfara ‘one who goes under compulsion’, tidfara ‘wanderer of time’, nifara ‘newcomer, stranger’, nige-cerred, -cumen, -hwirfed, -hworfen, niwan come (Beda II 1), -cumen. In the 13th-cent. manor the adventicius, forinsecus, extraneus may not move in without the permission of the lord of the manor, but is first conducted to the demesne farm; Vinogradoff Villainage 159. 142f. Cf. Gl Dorf 5b
‘farm’ (Kemble), ‘Ort’ Schmid, nicht ‘Domänengehöft’ im engeren Sinne
‘farm’ (Kemble), ‘place’ Schmid, not ‘demesne farmstead’ in the narrower sense
Vgl. Gl Kirchenpfennig 4. a. 10; o. 1, 1¹⁰
Cf. Gl Kirchenpfennig 4. a. 10; above 1, 1¹⁰

So Andrews, Larking; dagegen ‘zur Landeswache (wie 1, 1⁸) helfen’ Leo. Oft begegnet freilich inward ⁊ avera (o.⁵) als staatliche Grundlast im Domesday (Archiv Stud. neu. Spra. 109, 79); und auf dem Kossäten (s. u. 3, 4³·⁴) lasten solche Dienste zugunsten des Königs, nicht des Gutsherrn. Da aber sagt Verf. das deutlich

So Andrews, Larking; by contrast ‘help with the guarding of the land (as 1, 1⁸)’ Leo. It is true that inward ⁊ avera (above ⁵) often occurs as a public burden on land in Domesday (Archiv Stud. neu. Spra. 109, 79); and on the cottar (see below 3, 4³·⁴) such services are laid in favour of the king, not of the lord of the manor. But there the author says so clearly

‘Gestütswache’ Leo. Vielleicht nicht ein blosser Rosshirt (horshirde bei Ælfric), da die Hirten weiter unten vorkommen, sondern, gemäss dem voranstehenden halb kriegerischen Gefolgsamte und folgenden Botenauftrage, als herrschaftlicher ‘Stallmeister oder Marschall’ (vgl. Gl: horswealh), wie in höherer Gesellschaftsschicht ein horsþegn vorkommt

‘guarding of the stud’ Leo. Perhaps not a mere horse-herd (horshirde in Ælfric), since the herdsmen occur further below, but rather, in keeping with the semi-military retainer's duty that precedes and the errand duty that follows, a seigneurial ‘master of the horse or marshal’ (cf. Gl: horswealh), just as a horsþegn occurs in a higher social stratum
Vgl. Gl Bote 1. 5. a. In der folg. Zeile bessere Übs.: ‘ferner wie näher’
Cf. Gl Bote 1. 5. a. In the following line correct the transl. to ‘ferner wie näher’
